knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Break-even covers fixed costs using the contribution each session makes, so fixed costs divided by contribution per session is correct.
Implied credentials mislead clients. A descriptive name and a simple logo are recommended.
Timing gaps between income and costs can cause a cash shortfall even when the business is profitable on paper.
The break-even and cash flow section says fixed costs include rent, insurance and software, and venue hire per session is a variable cost.

practicalCriteria: The learner completes a name check record for three names, and the assessor confirms each check has a result
The learner calculates break-even sessions from supplied fixed costs and contribution, and the assessor recalculates the result
The learner builds a three-month cash-flow table and lists every point that needs a source, with an owner
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: List of points needing a source, with owners
stopWorkCriteria: Stop use of any name that implies a qualification or affiliation
Stop trading decisions that depend on a tax or insurance point without checking it
